new_statements.quote: Previous work on Nuni tones has been done by Flik (1979) who established the existence of three contrastive tones and Yago (1984) who described the tone system and established tone patterns on simple nouns and verbs. There are three contrastive tones in Nuni, H (high), M (mid), and L (low), represented here by an acute accent, unmarked, and a grave accent respectively. The three tones contrast on one syllable verbs in frames like the following: ... The same tones contrast on two syllable nouns in frames like the following: ... H and M downdrift after L tones in the usual way.
new_statements.citation: Kurrle, Gertrud. 1988. Some word tone patterns in Nuni. Journal of West African Languages 18(1): 29-40.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Nuni (Basinyari dialect) is described as a three-level tone language (H, M, L contrast lexically on verbs and nouns, with downdrift); the article says nothing about word stress or accent, so no stress-placement rule can be extracted from any source opened.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress; dialect differences (Léo vs Basinyari) concern tone patterns and vowel length only.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on words in frame sentences; no word- or phrase-level stress discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Kurrle 1988 describes the Basinyari dialect of (Southern) Nuni, fieldwork based in Léo, with notes on Léo-dialect differences — squarely sout2795. Caution for the wishlist: Prost 1971/1999 'nuni de Pouni' is tagged [nnw] in Glottolog's 1971 record, but Malgoubri 2011 (per Glottolog lgcode) classes Pouni as 'Yatini du Nord = Northern Nuni [nuv]' (nort2784); Nébié's works (1980 'Le ton en nuni', 1982 thesis, 1985 grammar) concern Northern Nuni per Berthelette 2002:12.

sources.quote: Previous work on Nuni tones has been done by Flik (1979) who established the existence of three contrastive tones and Yago (1984) who described the tone system and established tone patterns on simple nouns and verbs. There are three contrastive tones in Nuni, H (high), M (mid), and L (low), represented here by an acute accent, unmarked, and a grave accent respectively. The three tones contrast on one syllable verbs in frames like the following: ... The same tones contrast on two syllable nouns in frames like the following: ... H and M downdrift after L tones in the usual way.
sources.note: Nothing. States three contrastive tones (H, M, L) contrasting on monosyllabic verbs and disyllabic nouns, downdrift, tone patterns on verbs/nouns/compounds; note 3 gives the segment inventory (10 vowels, ATR harmony, length). No mention of stress or accent (the word 'accent' occurs only for tone diacritics).
